instruction.text: Select the history book about Boudica.
instruction.sound: Select the history book about Boodika.

feedback.finish: We don’t know a lot about Boudica’s life because only one person wrote about her at the time!

atoms.b: Tacitus was a Roman ((++historian geographer)) that was alive at the same time as Boudica.
As a Roman, he only told the ((++Roman Celtic)) side of the story.
When historians twist the ((++truth tooth)) or exaggerate certain things, it is called bias.

finish.text: Boudica might not have even been her real name! This is just what Tacitus called her. “Bouda” was a Celtic word meaning “victory”.
finish.sound: Boudica might not have even been her real name! This is just what Tacitus called her. “Bouda” was a Keltic word meaning “victory”.

atoms.b: and the Romans stayed in power.
atoms.sound: Ultimately, Boudica’s revolt was unsuccessful, and the Romans stayed in power.

atoms.b: that the Celts wouldn’t go out without a fight.
atoms.sound: However, the Romans now knew that the Kelts wouldn’t go out without a fight.

atoms.b: Today, Boudica is one of the most ((++famous disliked)) figures in British history.
The fight for her ((++land ocean)) has been inspirational for many people, especially women.

text: The Suffragettes, who fought for women to be allowed to vote, even put Boudica on some of their banners when protesting!

hint.text: More than one answer can be correct.

atoms.a: Why do you think there is a statue of Boudica and her daughters in London?
